concepts.quote: For a 3 × 3 board I would use a[0].length, but for any 2-D array I need a[i].length.
concepts.why: The answer gives each row its own length, which implies that rows are separate arrays and can differ in length (a ragged array), but it does not say this outright.

concepts.quote: for any 2-D array I need a[i].length
concepts.why: For new code that must work on any 2-D array, it correctly uses a[i].length as each row's bound instead of a fixed a[0].length.
It uses a[i] to mean a row but never says why or how indexing works, so it only names the element.
The answer does not mention arrays with three or more dimensions.
